A.text: In a red blood cell, $\text{CO}_2$ can combine with haemoglobin to form haemoglobinic acid.

B.text: Carbonic anhydrase is an enzyme that catalyses the reaction between $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

C.text: At the lungs, carbon dioxide is released when carbonic acid and water react together.

D.text: The greater the concentration of $\text{CO}_2$ in the blood, the higher the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen.
